date_scope_check.qualification: SA028-FU1: China MFA distinguishes cargo resumption on April 1, 2022 from ordinary passenger permission on April 3, 2023 and records temporary emergency passage. APP on April 5 confirms restored passenger clearance; its November 8 report counts over 40,000 passenger movements since April 3. Thus reopening is supported beyond a future announcement, although an independently observed first traveller is not identified. Profit's March and May 2021 reports describe the missed April 1, 2020 seasonal reopening and a May 31, 2021 opening for trade and travel based on ministry correspondence. The latter lacks a first ordinary passenger observation and prevents treating all 2020–2023 travel as unquestionably prohibited. The contemporary 2020 accounts and prolonged pandemic restriction support >24-hour eligibility, while onset, intervening permissions and the full continuous duration remain unresolved. Routine winter shutdowns, restricted cargo openings and emergency personnel passage must remain distinct. The April 3 passenger endpoint is retained without creating an uninterrupted whole-border interval.
